summary: Twelve comment-endorsed books, learning resources, developer tools, and independent services from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: The Idea Factory
items.summary: Jon Gertner's history of Bell Labs and its foundational inventions.
items.why_included: A commenter enthusiastically recommended it as a history of Bell Labs.
items.evidence: The commenter called the Bell Labs history an awesome book.

evidence_sources.author: kolinko
evidence_sources.excerpt: Awesome book about the history if Bell Labs - virtually all semiconductor tech we use today was created there

items.name: This Is Not Propaganda
items.summary: Peter Pomerantsev's book about modern disinformation and the war against reality.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly urged readers to consult this excellent book on propaganda.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the book for understanding Russian disinformation efforts.

evidence_sources.author: squidbeak
evidence_sources.excerpt: you ought to read Peter Pomerantsev's excellent "This is Not Propaganda"

items.name: Logic: An Introduction to Elementary Logic
items.summary: Wilfrid Hodges' accessible introduction to formal logic for beginners.
items.why_included: A commenter highly recommended it for laypeople starting from the beginning.
items.evidence: The commenter named Hodges' book among two highly recommended introductions to logic.

evidence_sources.author: rramadass
evidence_sources.excerpt: I highly recommend the following two books to study Logic from the beginning (for a layman); Logic: An Introduction to Elementary Logic by Wilfrid Hodges.

items.name: Bodily Oddities
items.summary: An indie catalog of strange, relatable quirks of the human body.
items.why_included: A commenter gave the site an unusually strong independent endorsement.
items.evidence: The commenter called the website fantastic and said the world was better for it.

evidence_sources.author: echelon
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love this website. It's fantastic. I don't care if it's AI. The world is better for it existing.

items.name: Usenet Rewind
items.summary: A search engine for exploring historical posts from early Usenet archives.
items.why_included: A user immediately recovered personally meaningful posts with it.
items.evidence: The commenter found old personal posts and called the discoveries cool.

evidence_sources.author: msephton
evidence_sources.excerpt: Just found some cool old stuff thanks to this:

items.name: Neal Nanda's Transformer Circuits Walkthrough
items.source_story_title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits (2021)
items.summary: A detailed video walkthrough of the transformer-circuits mathematical framework.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as a good detailed guide to difficult material.
items.evidence: The commenter praised the walkthrough while noting that its length reflects the topic's complexity.

evidence_sources.author: robrenaud
evidence_sources.excerpt: Neal Nanda's walkthrough of it is pretty good.

items.name: Loom
items.summary: A Rust tool that explores permutations of concurrent test executions.
items.why_included: A commenter strongly praised Loom's unusually approachable concurrency testing.
items.evidence: The commenter called Loom amazing and contrasted it with more cumbersome C and C++ tooling.

evidence_sources.author: mdspan
evidence_sources.excerpt: Loom is such an amazing project. I was always surprised by the fact that similar tooling for C/C++ is much more cumbersome to use

items.name: Inverse Kinematics and Foot Locking
items.summary: A technical reference on stable character feet and inverse-kinematics run cycles.
items.why_included: A commenter ranked it among the best references on a poorly documented topic.
items.evidence: The commenter praised it as an unusually strong reference for run cycles and foot locking.

evidence_sources.author: mmastrac
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is one of the best references on this topic I've seen - run cycles and foot locking are annoyingly lacking in documentation outside a few papers.

items.name: Galene
items.source_story_title: Linux Zoom client proactively reading everything written to X11 clipboard
items.summary: A lightweight, self-hosted videoconferencing server that supports standard browsers.
items.why_included: A user reported easy setup and reliable operation on an unsupported platform.
items.evidence: The commenter runs Galene on OpenBSD and said it just works.

evidence_sources.author: somat
evidence_sources.excerpt: Very easy to set up, I run it on obsd(an unsupported platform) and it just works.

items.name: Jitsi Meet
items.source_story_title: Linux Zoom client proactively reading everything written to X11 clipboard
items.summary: A free, open-source platform for browser-based video meetings.
items.why_included: A commenter directly endorsed it as an excellent open-source Zoom alternative.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended Jitsi as a free and open-source alternative.

evidence_sources.author: rascul
evidence_sources.excerpt: Jitsi is an excellent free and open source alternative.

items.name: Buildprof
items.source_story_title: I made a build visualizer to understand Bun's compile times
items.summary: A build visualizer for understanding where Bun compilation time is spent.
items.why_included: A developer praised its depth and presentation and planned to try it.
items.evidence: The commenter found Buildprof more comprehensive than their own tooling and intended to evaluate it.

evidence_sources.author: applfanboysbgon
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have some rudimentary tooling I threw together myself but nothing that looks as comprehensive and insightfully presented as this, I'll be giving it a try!

items.name: OpenStreetMap iD Editor
items.source_story_title: Make your first edit to OpenStreetMap
items.summary: OpenStreetMap's browser editor for quick, approachable map corrections.
items.why_included: A first-time contributor highly recommended it after a useful ten-minute edit.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the web editor as the easier path for first-time contributors.

evidence_sources.author: jkingsman
evidence_sources.excerpt: Would highly recommend the web editor -- what's proposed here looks super comprehensive but way more difficult to use for a first timer.
